title: Dropbox Shares How Its In-House Cookie Auditor Tests Consent Behaviour Across 200+ Web Surfaces
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/dropbox-cookie-auditor/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794331089979.jpg"/><p>Dropbox engineers described a Playwright-based auditor that checks cookie consent behavior across more than 200 web surfaces. It runs three tests per page: US visitor, EU visitor, and Global Privacy Control signal. Cookie rules are kept outside the code. A companion tool finds live URLs. Weekly reports separate likely violations from false positives.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

title: Effect 4.0 Ships: Dependency-Free Rewrite with 5x Smaller Bundles and Long-Term Support
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/effect-4-0-release/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794245718049.jpg"/><p>Effect 4.0, a TypeScript framework for typed errors and structured concurrency, was released on 30 September 2026 with a rewritten fiber runtime. The team reports a bundle size drop from 35.6 kB to 7.1 kB and about 6.4x higher throughput, though these figures are not independently verified. It also adds long-term support through September 2029.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

title: TypeScript 7.1 Beta: Restores the Compiler API and Makes Vue and Svelte First-Class
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/typescript-7-1-beta/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793901816316.jpg"/><p>TypeScript 7.1 Beta, announced October 20, 2026, restores the compiler API removed in 7.0, now split into separate entry points. It adds content mappers, letting tools like Vue check non-standard files. One Vue project's type checks fell from 14.19 to 3.10 seconds. An editor issue remains open, and teams may need TypeScript 6 alongside 7.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>
